name: Bhanu's Kitchen
signature_dish: Panasa manji bhaja (jackfruit-shoot stir-fry) with mandia rice
must_try: mandia kandul raav (millet flour with pigeon peas)
why_it_matters: Named by the Ministry of Tourism's Incredible India culinary guide as the only Koraput-town restaurant that serves the tribal-belt signature panasa manji bhaja (a jackfruit-tree-shoot dish that disappears outside Koraput district). One of two restaurants the government tourism portal credits by name for Koraput cuisine. Mandia (finger millet) is plated as ruti, raav and porridge — the staple grain of the Bonda, Paroja and Gadaba tribes, almost impossible to find at restaurant-grade hygiene elsewhere in Odisha.
insider_tip: Ask for the day's tribal special — Bhanu rotates by week based on what local Koraput haat vendors bring. The jackfruit-shoot dish is seasonal (Apr-Jun); mandia ruti is year-round. Don't expect English menu — point at neighbouring tables if needed.

name: Twin Bean Cafe — Dream Hill Coffee Estate
why_it_matters: Cafe inside the Dream Hill Coffee plantation in Koraput — the same arabica beans that Blue Tokai and Koraput Coffee Co-operative now sell across India. Coffee cultivation in Koraput was started by King Rajbahadur Rama Chandra Deo in the 1930s; this estate is among the modern revivers. Visitors get an estate walk under the shade trees (tribal Bonda and Paroja families nurture the plants) and a fresh brew at the source — no other coffee origin in Odisha is open to the public this way.
insider_tip: Phone +91 8637277174 before driving up — the estate is rain-fed and the cafe shuts during monsoon storms (Jul-Aug). Mornings are best; the harvest demo happens before noon during Nov-Feb season.
signature_address: Dream Hill Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha 764020

name: Ambica Restaurant
why_it_matters: Highest-rated restaurant in Koraput town on Tripadvisor (4.3 / 5) and ranked #2 in Koraput district overall. The default sit-down lunch and dinner for travellers when tribal-cuisine fatigue sets in — clean kitchen, predictable Indian menu, fair pricing. Reviewers single out chicken dishes and dum biryani as the strongest plates.
insider_tip: Lunch by 1 PM weekdays — Koraput's NALCO Damanjodi office crowd fills it from 1:15. Biryani is half-portion-shareable; order one between two if doing tribal lunch second.

name: Hotel Basanta Vilash Restaurant
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor-listed Koraput-town hotel restaurant (3.5 / 5) — the budget alternative to Ambica for the same Odia / north-Indian menu. Convenient if you're staying in the Koraput RWS / DM-office side of town and don't want to drive 2km to Ambica.
insider_tip: Ask if mandia ruti is on — the kitchen makes it some days, not always on the printed menu. Lunch is more reliable than dinner here.

name: Onkadelli Tribal Haat — Thursday Market
area: Onkadelli village, Odisha-AP border, ~65km from Koraput town
signature_dish: Bonda-tribe weekly haat — mahua liquor, jungle produce, salli (bamboo chicken)
why_it_matters: Thursday weekly haat of the Bonda — among India's most endangered tribal groups (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group / PVTG status). 9 AM to 2 PM only, one day a week. The only food market in Koraput where you'll see country chicken cooked salli-style (in green bamboo over fire) and mahua-flower spirit traded openly. Photography norms vary — Bonda women are private; ask via permit-holder. Cited by Outlook Traveller and Maverickbird as the most distinctive food-anthropology stop in Eastern Ghats.
insider_tip: Hire a Koraput-based guide who has worked the market — entering without one risks photo confrontations and zero hospitality. Plan to leave Onkadelli by 2 PM; tribal groups walk back to their hilltop villages and the road empties.
signature_address: Onkadelli weekly haat, Odisha-Andhra border, Pottangi tehsil, Koraput district, Odisha 764039
